blocks.prompt: 15. If \(p\)th, \(q\)th terms of a G.P. are \(q\) and \(p\) respectively, show that \((p + q)\)th term is \(\left(q^{p} \div p^{q}\right)^{\frac{1}{p - q}}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof with letters: two terms are given, a third must be shown equal to an expression.
We need \(a_{p+q} = a_1 r^{p+q-1}\).
Plan: divide the two equations to get \(r\); then write \(a_{p+q} = a_p \cdot r^{q}\) and simplify the indices.
steps:
Given: \(a_p = q\), \(a_q = p\) (\(p \neq q\)).
To prove: \(a_{p+q} = (q^p \div p^q)^{\frac{1}{p-q}}\).
Method: Find \(r\) by dividing; then move \(q\) places forward from \(a_p\).

Write the two given terms
\[a_1 r^{p-1} = q \quad (1)\]
\[a_1 r^{q-1} = p \quad (2)\]
Why: \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) with \(n = p\) and \(n = q\).

Divide (1) by (2)
\[r^{(p-1)-(q-1)} = \dfrac{q}{p}\]
\[r^{p-q} = \dfrac{q}{p}\]
\[r = \left(\dfrac{q}{p}\right)^{\frac{1}{p-q}}\]
Why: \(a_1\) cancels and the indices subtract. Raising both sides to the power \(\frac{1}{p-q}\) leaves \(r\).

Move \(q\) places on from \(a_p\)
\[a_{p+q} = a_1 r^{p+q-1}\]
\[= \left(a_1 r^{p-1}\right) r^{q} = q\, r^{q}\]
Why: \(p + q - 1 = (p - 1) + q\), and \(a_1 r^{p-1} = q\) from (1).

Put in \(r\)
\[q\, r^{q} = q \left(\dfrac{q}{p}\right)^{\frac{q}{p-q}}\]
\[= \dfrac{q^{1 + \frac{q}{p-q}}}{p^{\frac{q}{p-q}}}\]
Why: A power of a power multiplies: \(\left(x^{1/(p-q)}\right)^{q} = x^{q/(p-q)}\).

Combine the indices of \(q\)
\[1 + \dfrac{q}{p - q} = \dfrac{p - q + q}{p - q}\]
\[= \dfrac{p}{p - q}\]
Why: Write 1 as \(\frac{p-q}{p-q}\) and add the tops.

Write in the required form
\[a_{p+q} = \dfrac{q^{\frac{p}{p-q}}}{p^{\frac{q}{p-q}}}\]
\[= \left(\dfrac{q^{p}}{p^{q}}\right)^{\frac{1}{p-q}}\]
\[= \left(q^{p} \div p^{q}\right)^{\frac{1}{p-q}}\]
Why: Both indices have the factor \(\frac{1}{p-q}\), so take it outside the bracket.

Check with numbers
\[p = 2, q = 1:\ a_2 = 1,\ a_1 = 2\]
\[r = \tfrac{1}{2},\ a_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[(1^2 \div 2^1)^{1} = \tfrac{1}{2}\ \checkmark\]
Why: For the G.P. \(2, 1, \frac{1}{2}, \ldots\) the formula gives the true 3rd term.
